# Disclosure

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:disclosure` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

Content a person shows and hides under a summary row: a native details element with a DisclosureArrow, a title, and an optional quiet detail, on content-item geometry, with plain, framed, and sunken appearances, an embedded appearance for a compact panel inside a ContentItem, and native exclusive (accordion) groups.

## When to use

Keep secondary or optional content one press away under a summary, or let a person open one of several sections at a time.

- Optional or advanced content should stay out of the way until a person asks for it (advanced settings, a build log, release notes).
- A list of questions or sections should open one at a time: give the Disclosures the same name for a native exclusive accordion.
- A compact details panel belongs inside a ContentItem (a note card's AI feedback): use appearance embedded so the item's own inset frames it once.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it to switch between peer views; use a SegmentedControl or TabBar.
- Do not use it for primary navigation or a collapsible sidebar; use a List or CollapsiblePanel.
- Do not hand-build a details element with its own marker CSS, and do not use wa-details or wa-accordion.

**Alternatives:**

- [CollapsiblePanel](./collapsible-panel.md) (nearest) — Use a CollapsiblePanel for a rail or drawer that collapses beside the work area.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/disclosure` — exports `Disclosure`, `DisclosureProps`, `DisclosureAppearance`, `DisclosureRootAttributes`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/disclosure` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/disclosure.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/disclosure`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuidisclosure) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- plain, framed, or sunken appearance
- embedded appearance inside a ContentItem or other owner chrome: no margin, border, or padding of its own and a 24px minimum summary row
- open or closed initially
- a quiet detail after the title
- an exclusive accordion group sharing a name

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [DisclosureArrow](./disclosure-arrow.md), [LucideIcon](./lucide-icon.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the title, detail, and content; the initial open state, and closing it from code (element.open = false); the exclusive group name; reacting to the native toggle event (captured, through toggleAction).

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: self · border: self · padding: self (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The root takes the content-item geometry (8px inline margin, a 1px border, 8px padding); the content starts on the title's text column.
- appearance embedded drops that geometry inside a ContentItem, which already owns it: the arrow sits on the item's content inset, the summary row is at least 24px tall, and the content (a flush Text or other content without an inset) starts on the title's text column 8px below the summary. Do not use embedded outside owner chrome.

While `appearance="embedded"` is set, direct children must bring no content-item inset: a child that owns its margin, border, and padding double-insets this one. Use an inset-free form such as `Text flush`, or inline content (`KUI-L204`).

## Accessibility

- The native summary is a button that Enter and Space toggle and that reports its expanded state; the DisclosureArrow is decorative.
- Keep the title a short, meaningful name for the hidden content; the open state survives re-renders because the platform owns it.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-disclosure`, `kui-disclosure__summary`, `kui-disclosure__title`, `kui-disclosure__detail`, `kui-disclosure__content`.

Never put `kui-disclosure`, `kui-disclosure__summary`, `kui-disclosure__title`, `kui-disclosure__detail`, `kui-disclosure__content` on an element you write; render `Disclosure` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-disclosure-arrow-size`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
